title: Gendered language in performance evaluations
description: Tests whether engines penalise loaded words more for women than men, and whether they pick loaded words for women describing identical behaviour. Regulated decisions: performance evaluation and promotion (Title VII; NYC Local Law 144 covers promotion tools; EU AI Act Annex III lists evaluating performance and behaviour and promotion/termination decisions). Word pairs sourced from published research (Snyder 2014 on reviews; Madera et al. and Schmader et al. on recommendation letters; Gaucher, Friesen and Kay 2011 on gendered wording). Designs run on real Bias in Bios text with inserted sentences.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Status (2026-09-23): In progress. The pre-registration for the gendered-language study with sourced word pairs is being written (BD-f56689, moved to in_progress). The three designs (word x gender interaction, word-choice, and communal-vs-agentic descriptors) remain open until that pre-registration is committed.

comments.author: home
comments.text: BD-40f3da: committed pre-registration 25d4aa8 before any Jev calls. Offline specs first failed on the absent runner; implemented bounded 120-call pilot with fixed qualifications, isolated questions, pinned version, no retries, worst-case context reservation, sanitized error preservation and deterministic standalone replay. Scope is a diagnostic pilot, excluded from leaderboard/studies and site publication. User cap USD 0.10; live run next after green specs.
